summary.overview: The recall project has a strong local validation suite and well-structured agent guidance, but three gaps prevent these mechanisms from being wired into ordinary delivery: no CI quality gate enforces test, lint, or format checks on pull requests; the self-update command replaces the binary with no rollback path; and AGENTS.md carries a stale ticket count that no longer matches the repository.
strengths: Six distinct test layers (unit, integration, golden queries, contract, error, snapshot) with tempfile-based per-test database isolation
Well-structured AGENTS.md with workspace-layout responsibility table, command surface, and architecture summary
Runtime crash safety via SQLite WAL mode, exclusive file lock with auto-release, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md provides a clear context map and workspace layout, but carries a stale ticket count and lacks risk-route mapping for core files.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Build, test, and doctor commands are documented with WAL-mode crash safety, but no permission boundary, toolchain pin, or sandbox constrains agent operations.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Six local test layers cover the main change paths, but no CI step enforces test, lint, or format checks before merge or release.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: A cargo-dist release pipeline exists, but no CI quality gate, approval boundary, or rollback path protects merges or the self-update command.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: No comparable session evidence is available in this window; a bounded review was completed but no recurring opportunity or later outcome can be supported.

findings.title: Pull requests and releases are not mechanically checked for test passage, lint, or format compliance
findings.reason: The project documents cargo test (81 tests), cargo clippy, and cargo fmt as local commands, and the release workflow at .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on pull_request and version-tag pushes, but its jobs are exclusively cargo-dist build and release stages (plan, build-local-artifacts, build-global-artifacts, host, announce). No cargo test, cargo clippy, or cargo fmt --check step exists in any CI workflow. An agent or human can introduce failing tests or lint violations without CI blocking the merge or release. Host-side branch protection or required checks were not inspected and may exist as GitHub settings not visible in the repository.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Workflow owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Add a CI quality gate to the release workflow or a new workflow that runs cargo test, cargo clippy, and cargo fmt --check on pull requests before merge.

## Validation

- Trigger the workflow on pull_request
- Confirm all three checks pass or report exact failures

findings.title: Self-update replaces the running binary with no dry-run, approval prompt, or rollback path
findings.reason: The recall update command in src/update.rs downloads a binary from GitHub and atomically replaces the running executable. On Unix, it writes to a .tmp file then renames over the current executable; on Windows, it renames the current to .old, writes the new binary, and deletes the old one. No --dry-run flag, no confirmation prompt, and no rollback documentation precedes the replacement. If the new binary is broken, there is no automatic rollback path on Unix because the old binary is overwritten by the rename. The update check itself is non-blocking and only prints a notice; replacement happens only on explicit recall update invocation, which bounds the risk to intentional use.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Code owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Add a rollback or backup-binary mechanism to the recall update command so a failed update can be reversed.

## Validation

- Run recall update --dry-run to preview the replacement without executing
- Confirm a backup of the previous binary is retained or a rollback command exists

findings.title: AGENTS.md states a ticket count that no longer matches the repository
findings.reason: AGENTS.md line 35 states .tickets/ — work tracking (23 tickets, 19 done), but the .tickets/ directory currently contains 39 ticket files (01 through 39) plus config.toml. This is a deterministic factual contradiction between the instruction file and the current repository state. An agent reading AGENTS.md receives stale scope information about the project work tracking volume. The done sub-count (19) cannot be verified without reading individual ticket contents, but the total count (23 vs 39) is deterministically stale.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
Update the ticket count in AGENTS.md to match the current .tickets/ directory contents.

## Validation

- Count the ticket files in .tickets/
- Confirm AGENTS.md reflects the actual count
